Alright, I'm in the middle of refining the Taj Mahal model. I've already made several edits to the index.html to improve geometry placements and orientations. The latest change I applied was to the flanking niches on the side walls, simplifying their dimensions and adjusting offsets. Now I need to address another set of architectural details that still look slightly off.

Looking at the current code (though I haven't re-read the whole file, I recall the relevant snippet), there is a loop that creates a pair of arches or decorative elements for each side of the central structure. The loop iterates over two levels (`lvl` of `[0, BODY_H / 2]`) and creates an arched panel with dimensions `(10.5, BODY_H / 2 - 1.2, 1.3, 3.4, 10)`. After positioning the panel at `c.x, PLINTH_TOP + lvl + 0.6, c.z` and setting its rotation to `c.ry`, the panel is added directly to the `taj` group.

When I preview the scene, these panels appear to be slightly recessed relative to the surrounding walls—they're not quite flush with the façade. The visual reference (the real Taj Mahal) shows that these decorative arches should project just a hair outward from the wall surface, creating a subtle depth. My current code places them exactly on the wall plane, which makes the edges look flat and the geometry looks a bit sunken.

To fix this, I need to nudge each panel outward a tiny amount along its local forward axis. Since the panels are oriented by setting `rotation.y = c.ry`, their forward direction corresponds to the local positive Z axis after rotation. In Three.js, I can achieve a small forward translation by calling `translateZ` on the mesh. A translation of about 0.03 units should be enough to create that subtle extrusion without breaking the overall proportions.

I must be careful not to alter any other properties. The loop already sets position and rotation; adding a `translateZ(0.03)` after those statements will move the mesh forward in its own coordinate space. I will insert this line right before `taj.add(n);` to keep the transformation order correct (position, rotation, then translation).

Now I need to construct the edit operation. The `old_string` should match the exact block I'm replacing: the loop with the four lines inside. The `new_string` will be the same block but with the additional `n.translateZ(0.03);` line inserted. I will keep the formatting identical to avoid any mismatches.

Thus, the appropriate tool call is an Edit on `index.html`, replacing the old snippet with the new one that includes the translation. This small tweak should resolve the visual issue and bring the model closer to the intended cinematic quality.
